findings.title: Render branches have no direct tests
findings.description: `_product_lines` has several branches: no tier configured, edge never observed, `caught_up` of `None` or holed, and "contracts: none with ingested records yet". `age()` is also untested. A grep of `test/` found no unit test importing `tick_status_render`, and none of those strings appear in the new tests. The integration tests (`test_tick_status_cli.py`) only exercise the single "ingested, tier-less, edge-less" path. The "no contracts" message came from a late bug-fix commit and has no regression test, and `age()` (with its `divmod` arithmetic) has no boundary tests (0 s, 59 s, 1 h, 1 d). Pure string-building functions like these are cheap to parametrize. `print_coverage`'s mismatch lines are covered only through exit-code and "mismatch" substring checks.

findings.title: Import-time `assert` guards a runtime invariant
findings.description: The check that `_BUCKET_ROWS` covers every `TickSessionStatus` is a module-level `assert`. It is stripped under `python -O`, so a new status would then be silently dropped from the report. A failure also surfaces as an import error for the whole CLI. A unit test asserting the same set equality would enforce it without those problems. Alternatively, derive the layout from the enum.

findings.title: `shape_units` is queried twice per product
findings.description: `_product_status` calls `_scope`, which runs `shape_units(conn, shape_of(entry))`. It then calls `session_verdicts`, which runs the same query again. It also calls `contract_lines`, which re-joins the same unit/request/ledger set. The unit read is a full-shape scan with no date bound, so each product pays for it twice. Passing the first result into `session_verdicts` would remove the duplicate query and the chance of the two reads seeing different data.

findings.title: Loosened connection types at the read boundary
findings.description: `_read` takes `Callable[[Any, str], ...]`, and the inner `read(conn: Any, ...)` in `tick_coverage` is also `Any`. The project already defines `Conn = psycopg.AsyncConnection[Any]` in `manifest_reads`. Using it here keeps strict pyright able to check the callbacks. `_read_storage()` exists only to lazily import one class, and it adds indirection. The same lazy import could sit inline in `tick_status` and `tick_coverage`, or `TickDatabaseUnreachable` could be passed directly.

findings.title: `run_mapped` storage override is order-dependent
findings.description: `TickDatabaseUnreachable` subclasses `TickPreflightError`, so `exit_code_for` still returns exit 1 for it in the writers. The read verbs get exit 4 only because they pass a `storage` tuple to `run_mapped`. Exit-code mapping is now split between `tick_exit.exit_code_for` and a per-call override, which cuts against the "defined once, in `tick_exit.py`" statement in the module docstring. Handling the subclass in `exit_code_for` would keep one source of truth. The writers would need a decision on whether unreachable means exit 1 or 4 there too. The behaviour is tested and the override is documented, so this is a design smell and not a bug.

findings.title: Spread filtering uses O(n²) list membership
findings.description: `[c for c in lines if c not in spreads]` does a dataclass-equality list scan per contract. The counts are small, but filtering with `c.instrument_class != SPREAD_CLASS` is simpler and avoids the issue.

findings.title: Function and docstring sizes
findings.description: `_product_status` is about 50 lines, at the project's soft limit. Several public render and build helpers (`print_status`, `coverage_to_dict`, `print_coverage`, `build_status`, `shape_of`, `jsonable`) have no docstrings. Both are minor.

findings.title: SQL, DB safety, and refactors
findings.description: All queries are parameterized. The only f-string interpolations are module constants (`_UNITS`, `COVERAGE_PREDICATE`), not user input. The read verbs use `connect_migrated` with no lock and no destructive statements. The test deletes target throwaway fixture databases and use primary keys instead of `ctid`, as the in-test comments explain. The raw-count window (`BETWEEN` on session open and close) matches the ingest worker's bounds in `ingest_worker.py`. The `utc_midnight` and `days_touched` extraction in `session_days.py` removes duplicate logic, and `ingest_plan.py` now reuses it. The `except Exception` in `run_mapped` is a documented process-boundary handler that re-raises unmapped errors. Integration tests cover exit codes 0, 1, 3 and 4, and JSON parity with `to_dict()`.

structured_findings.summary: Render branches have no direct tests
Loosened connection types at the read boundary
Spread filtering uses O(n²) list membership
